paper.title: Bandits with Abstention under Expert Advice

settings.name_in_paper: Prediction with expert advice under bandit feedback with an abstention action
unmapped: K+1 actions, one of which (abstention) has zero reward on every trial

experts are confidence-rated predictors (sub-probability vectors over K actions); comparator is any nonnegative linear combination u of experts that yields a valid policy (u . c_t <= 1 for all t), not just a single expert
settings.definition_quote: In this problem we have $K+1$ actions, $E$ experts, and $T$ trials. On each trial $t$: Each expert suggests, to the learner, a probability distribution over the $K+1$ actions. The learner selects an action $a_t$. The reward incurred by action $a_t$ on trial $t$ (which is in $[-1,1]$) is revealed to the learner. ... we consider the case in which there is an action (the abstention action) that incurs zero reward on every trial.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial contextual bandits with abstention (finite context set, basis)
unmapped: abstention action with zero reward always available
finite context set; learner is given a basis (family of context subsets) a priori
comparator: policy that plays action b_j on disjoint basis elements B_j and abstains elsewhere
the learner knows the number M of comparator basis elements (used to tune eta and initial weights)
settings.definition_quote: In this problem, we have a finite set of contexts $\cons$. A-priori nature selects a sequence: $\seq{(x_t,\bs{r}_t)\in\cons\times[-1,1]^K}{t\in[T]}$, but does not reveal it to the learner. ... The context $x_t$ is revealed to the learner. The learner selects an action $a_t\in[K]\cup\{\square\}$. The learner sees and incurs reward $r_{t,a_t}\in[-1,1]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial contextual bandits with abstention (lower bound)
unmapped: abstention action with zero reward always available
finite context set with a basis given a priori; comparator plays b_j on disjoint basis elements B_j and abstains elsewhere
settings.definition_quote: Take any learning algorithm. Given any basis $\basis$ and any $M\in\mathbb{N}$, for any sequence of disjoint basis elements ... there exists a sequence of corresponding actions ... such that an adversary can force ...

symbols.Delta_u_w1: unnormalized relative entropy between comparator weight vector u (any valid nonnegative combination of experts) and initial weights w_1

conditions: comparator u in the set of nonnegative weight vectors such that u . c_t <= 1 for all t

source.label: cbath
source.quote: \ose\ takes parameters $\eta\in(0,1)$ and $\bs{w}_1\in\mathbb{R}_+^E$. For any $\bs{u}\in\val$ the expected cumulative reward of \ose\ is bounded below by: $\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}[r_{t,a_t}]\geq\expt{\trf(\bs{u})}- \frac{\Delta(\bs{u},\bs{w}_1)}{\eta}-\eta (12K+2)T$ ... The per-trial time complexity of \ose\ is in $\mathcal{O}(KE)$.

results.notes: Stated as a lower bound on reward; rearranged to regret vs the policy pi(u). Comparator is a linear combination of experts (generalizes best expert). Per-trial time O(KE). The algorithm does not use T unless eta is tuned, so horizon is marked anytime.

symbols.M_b: number of disjoint basis elements in the comparator policy

conditions: comparator: disjoint basis elements B_1..B_M with actions b_j; abstain outside their union

source.label: basisthm
source.quote: Given any basis $\basis$ of cardinality $N$ and any $M\in\mathbb{N}$ we can implement \ose\ such that for any sequence of disjoint basis elements ... we have: $\sum_{t\in[T]}\expt{r_{t,a_t}}\geq\sum_{t\in[T]}\sum_{j\in[M]}\indi{x_t\in\bll_j}r_{t,\cra{j}}-\sqrt{2M\ln(N)(6K+1)T}$. The per-trial time complexity ... $\mathcal{O}(KN)$.

results.notes: Per-trial time O(KN). Tuning requires M and T.

symbols.M_b: number of disjoint basis elements in the comparator policy

conditions: any basis and any sequence of M disjoint basis elements; actions b_j chosen adversarially; contexts chosen adversarially

source.quote: Take any learning algorithm. Given any basis $\basis$ and any $M\in\mathbb{N}$, for any sequence of disjoint basis elements $\seq{\bll_j}{j\in[M]}$ there exists a sequence of corresponding actions ... such that an adversary can force: ... $\in \Omega\left(\sqrt{MKT}\right)$.

results.notes: Restated as Proposition C.1 in the appendix, which has a sketch proof based on Auer et al. (2002) and Seldin & Lugosi (2016).

symbols.M_b: number of disjoint balls in the comparator policy

conditions: contexts form a metric space with distance known to the learner; basis is the set of metric balls
comparator: disjoint balls B_1..B_M with actions b_j; abstain elsewhere
tuning: implementation with binary-tree data structure; parameters tuned as in Corollary 5.1

source.label: ballth
source.quote: Let $N:=|\cons|$. Given any $M\in\mathbb{N}$ we can implement \ose\ such that for any sequence of disjoint balls ... we have: $\sum_{t\in[T]}\expt{r_{t,a_t}}\geq\sum_{t\in[T]}\sum_{j\in[M]}\indi{x_t\in\bll_j}r_{t,\cra{j}}-\sqrt{4M\ln(N)(6K+1)T}$. The per-trial time complexity ... $\mathcal{O}(KN\ln(N))$.

symbols.U_sum: sum of comparator weights sum_j u_j over the (possibly overlapping) balls

conditions: basis is the set of metric balls in a metric known to the learner
weights u_j in [0,1] with sum_j 1[x in B_j] u_j <= 1 for all contexts x (balls may overlap)

source.label: thm:OBE4overlapping
source.quote: The regret of \ose, with the set of experts given in Section \ref{sec:efficientlearning} and with correctly tuned parameters, is then bounded by: $\sum_{t\in[T]}{r}^*_t-\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}[{r}_{t,a_t}]\in \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{\ln(KN)KT\sum_{j\in[M]}u_j}\right)$. Its per-trial time complexity is: $\mathcal{O}(KN\ln(N))$.

results.notes: Comparator is a weighted mix of overlapping balls. Theorem 5.3 is the special case with disjoint balls and u_j = 1.

cited_results.setting_description: Bandits with expert advice; regret relative to a comparator u with ||u||_1 = 1 (a distribution over experts)
Adversarial multi-armed bandit with K arms (one of them a known suboptimal abstention arm)
